# Design tokens

`@mpc/design` 0.1.0 · 44 tokens (38 CSS variables)

`tokens/*.json` is the only source. This document and the CSS, JSON, SCSS, and
Dart in `dist/` are all generated from it. `*` marks a reference-only value
that produces no CSS variable.

### Surfaces

Four depths, near-black and cool. Depth is carried by lightness alone — the site has no elevation shadows.

| Token | Value | Hex | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--background` | `oklch(0.13 0.02 265)` | #04070F | Page background. Every route sits on this. |
| `--foreground` | `oklch(0.96 0.005 250)` | #EFF2F5 | Body text on any dark surface. |
| `--surface` | `oklch(0.16 0.018 260)` | #090D15 | Section blocks that need to separate from the page.<br>**Note:** Often used at partial opacity (`bg-surface/40`) to soften the step between sections. |
| `--surface-elevated` | `oklch(0.19 0.02 260)` | #0F141D | The topmost surface: raised panels inside a section. |
| `--card` | `oklch(0.17 0.018 260)` | #0B1017 | shadcn card background.<br>**Note:** Darker than --surface-elevated despite both describing cards. Site sections use --surface-elevated; only shadcn primitives read this token. |
| `--card-foreground` | `oklch(0.96 0.005 250)` | #EFF2F5 | Text inside a shadcn card. |
| `--popover` | `oklch(0.17 0.018 260)` | #0B1017 | Floating surfaces: dropdown, popover, command, tooltip panels. |
| `--popover-foreground` | `oklch(0.96 0.005 250)` | #EFF2F5 | Text on floating surfaces. |

### Brand & interactive

Copper in its interface role: the accent a visitor can act on. Two near-identical values exist here for historical reasons — see the note on --primary.

| Token | Value | Hex | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--primary` | `oklch(0.72 0.12 55)` | #DE8F57 | shadcn's primary slot — what `Button`, `Switch`, and friends render.<br>**Note:** A third copper, lighter than --copper and not part of the published scale. Site components should reach for --copper; --primary exists so unmodified shadcn primitives stay on-brand. Worth reconciling. |
| `--primary-foreground` | `oklch(0.13 0.02 265)` | #04070F | Text on a copper fill. Near-black, not white — copper is too light to carry white text at AA. |
| `--copper` | `oklch(0.68 0.13 50)` | #D77E49 | The brand accent in the interface: eyebrow labels, links, emphasis, primary buttons.<br>**Note:** Published as Copper Light in the media kit. This is the value site components use directly (`bg-copper`, `text-copper`). |
| `--copper-glow` | `oklch(0.78 0.14 60)` | #F8A052 | Hover and active states only. Never a resting colour and never a large fill. |
| `--ring` | `oklch(0.72 0.12 55)` | #DE8F57 | Focus ring. Identical to --primary, so keyboard focus is unmistakably the brand accent. |

### Support pairs

Background/foreground pairs for secondary UI. Always used as a pair: a surface token without its -foreground partner is how contrast bugs start.

| Token | Value | Hex | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--secondary` | `oklch(0.22 0.02 260)` | #151B24 | Secondary button and badge fills. |
| `--secondary-foreground` | `oklch(0.92 0.005 250)` | #E2E5E8 | Text on --secondary. |
| `--muted` | `oklch(0.2 0.018 260)` | #11161E | Recessed blocks: table headers, skeletons, disabled fills. |
| `--muted-foreground` | `oklch(0.65 0.015 255)` | #899098 | Secondary text. Carries most body copy on this site — the sections lead with foreground headlines and muted paragraphs. |
| `--accent` | `oklch(0.25 0.025 260)` | #1B222E | Hover fill for menu and list items.<br>**Note:** Not a brand colour despite the name — it is shadcn's neutral hover slot. Brand accent is --copper. |
| `--accent-foreground` | `oklch(0.96 0.005 250)` | #EFF2F5 | Text on --accent. |

### Signal colours

Each carries a fixed meaning. Reaching for one because it looks right is the misuse this group exists to prevent.

| Token | Value | Hex | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--gold` | `oklch(0.82 0.11 80)` | #EABC6E | Figure emphasis — the number in a stat, not the label around it. |
| `--steppe` | `oklch(0.42 0.06 155)` | #31573F | Mongolian asset context. The only green that is not a status. |
| `--sand` | `oklch(0.78 0.07 75)` | #D2B285 | Secondary backgrounds in asset-context artwork. |
| `--positive` | `oklch(0.62 0.1 155)` | #50986B | Confirmed state — secured, verified, on-chain. Also the live-dot pulse. |
| `--alert` | `oklch(0.62 0.12 45)` | #C16D45 | Attention, not failure. Provisional and in-progress states. |
| `--destructive` | `oklch(0.55 0.18 25)` | #C53637 | Irreversible actions and hard errors.<br>**Note:** Red, and the only token outside the warm/neutral system. That is the point: it should look foreign. |
| `--destructive-text` | `oklch(0.64 0.15 25)` | #D8625C | Destructive meaning as text on a dark surface.<br>**Note:** A fill colour and a text colour cannot be the same swatch here. `destructive` is dark enough to carry near-white text on top of it (4.72:1), which is exactly why it fails as text on our dark surfaces (3.80:1 on background). This token is the lighter twin, and it is the one to reach for whenever the red is a word rather than a shape. |
| `--destructive-foreground` | `oklch(0.96 0.005 250)` | #EFF2F5 | Text on a destructive fill. |

### Lines & inputs

White at low alpha rather than a solid grey, so a hairline reads consistently on all four surface depths without a per-surface variant.

| Token | Value | Hex | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--border` | `oklch(1 0 0 / 8%)` | #FFFFFF | Default hairline. Applied globally to every element in @layer base.<br>**Note:** Alpha-channel white, so it never appeared in the generated hex palette. Use the .hairline-t / .hairline-b utilities rather than a raw border. |
| `--border-strong` | `oklch(1 0 0 / 16%)` | #FFFFFF | Emphasised divider where the default hairline disappears. |
| `--input` | `oklch(1 0 0 / 12%)` | #FFFFFF | Form field borders. Brighter than --border so an input reads as interactive. |

### Geometry

A deliberately tight radius scale. The largest value is 10px: the visual language is drawn with rules and hairlines, and rounded corners work against it.

| Token | Value | Hex | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--radius-sm` | `2px` | — | Badges, tags, inline chips. |
| `--radius-md` | `4px` | — | Buttons and inputs. The default. |
| `--radius-lg` | `6px` | — | Cards and panels. |
| `--radius-xl` | `10px` | — | Dialogs and sheets. The ceiling. |
| `--radius` | `4px` | — | Base radius consumed by shadcn primitives. |

### Type stacks

Self-hosted via @fontsource — there is no fonts.googleapis.com request. The fallbacks matter: they are what renders before the webfont resolves.

| Token | Value | Hex | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--font-sans` | `"Inter", system-ui, sans-serif` | — | Body copy and interface text. The document default. |
| `--font-display` | `"Space Grotesk", "Inter", sans-serif` | — | Headlines and figures. Always with -0.02em tracking via .font-display.<br>**Note:** Falls back to Inter, not a system serif — a headline that loses its webfont should still look like this site. |
| `--font-mono` | `"JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace, monospace` | — | Eyebrow labels and data. Never body copy. |

## Utility classes

Classes defined by `dist/utilities.css`. A ✓ in the **Motion** column means the
`prefers-reduced-motion` block disables that class by name.

| Class | Motion | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.font-display` |  | Display face plus the -0.02em tracking it is designed with. Use this, not `font-family` alone. |
| `.font-mono` |  | Mono face for data and labels. |
| `.label-eyebrow` |  | The eyebrow label: 11px mono, 0.18em tracking, uppercase, copper. Every section opens with one. |
| `.text-balance` |  | Balanced line breaks for headlines. Not for paragraphs. |
| `.hairline-t` |  | Top divider at --border. The standard way sections separate. |
| `.hairline-b` |  | Bottom divider at --border. |
| `.grid-lines` |  | Static 80px measuring grid. Structural texture, not decoration. |
| `.copper-gradient` |  | Copper-to-gold gradient clipped to text. Static counterpart to .copper-shimmer. |
| `.glow-copper` |  | Wide, low-opacity copper glow behind a focal element. |
| `.reveal` | ✓ | Scroll reveal. Pair with the Reveal component — the raw class stays invisible until .is-visible is added. |
| `.is-visible` |  | Applied by the Reveal observer. Never author this in JSX. Reduced-motion neutralises it through .reveal rather than by name. |
| `.grid-pan` | ✓ | The measuring grid, panning slowly. Backgrounds only. |
| `.copper-shimmer` | ✓ | Light travelling across a copper headline. One per page — it is the hero's device. |
| `.aurora` | ✓ | Drifting blurred colour field for ambient depth. Absolutely positioned, pointer-events: none. |
| `.flow-dash` | ✓ | Travelling dashes along an SVG path — flow direction in the pipeline diagram. |
| `.flow-particle` | ✓ | A particle riding an SVG path via offset-distance. |
| `.flow-rail` | ✓ | Sweep travelling across a horizontal rail. |
| `.node-pulse` | ✓ | Pulsing node in a diagram. Marks an active stage. |
| `.live-dot` | ✓ | Expanding ring in --positive. Reserved for genuinely live state. |
